The 2011–12 season was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]'s 98th competitive season, their 23rd consecutive season in the top flight of English [[association football|football]] (20th in the [[Premier League]]), and their 106th year in existence as a [[football club (association football)|football club]]. While their sixth place in the league was their lowest domestic finish since 2001–02, they completed a cup double by winning their seventh [[FA Cup]] and their first [[UEFA Champions League]].

==Key dates==
* 22 June 2011: [[André Villas-Boas]] is appointed as the new manager on a three-year contract, with immediate effect.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/jun/22/chelsea-confirm-andre-villas-boas|title=Chelsea appoint former Porto coach André Villas-Boas on three-year deal|date=22 June 2011|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=22 June 2011|first=Paul|last=Doyle}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2380210 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130804060856/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2380210 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 August 2013 |title=Villas-Boas appointed |publisher=Chelsea F.C |access-date=22 June 2011 }}</ref>
* 7 July 2011: Villas-Boas and the rest of the first team squad have their first training of the season together.<ref>{{Cite news |last=INM |title=Villas-Boas more Pep talk than Jose on first Chelsea team-building day |url=http://www.independent.co.uk:80/sport/football/premier-league/villasboas-more-pep-talk-than-jose-on-first-chelsea-teambuilding-day-2307968.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902095411/http://www.independent.co.uk:80/sport/football/premier-league/villasboas-more-pep-talk-than-jose-on-first-chelsea-teambuilding-day-2307968.html |archive-date=2011-09-02 |access-date=2025-08-15 |work=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>
* 13 July 2011: Chelsea win their first [[friendly match]] against [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].
* 26 July 2011: Chelsea confirm [[Thibaut Courtois]], a Belgian goalkeeper, as Villas-Boas' first signing. He is immediately loaned out to [[Atlético Madrid]] of [[La Liga]].<ref name="Courtois Relishing Challenge" />
* 14 August 2011: Chelsea draw first match of the [[Premier League]] season away to [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]]. It finishes 0–0 on Villas-Boas's debut as Chelsea manager.
* 20 August 2011: Villas-Boas wins his first competitive match as a Chelsea manager after Chelsea defeat [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] 2–1 at Stamford Bridge.
* 22 August 2011: Chelsea and [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] agree a deal for [[Juan Mata]], who signs for Chelsea for a fee rumoured to be £23.5 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2427778 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130804060834/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2427778 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 August 2013 |title=Mata deal agreed |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=22 August 2011 |access-date=2 August 2013 }}</ref>
* 27 August 2011: Juan Mata scores on his debut match in a 3–1 home victory against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].
* 27 August 2011: Chelsea and [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]] agree a deal for [[Ulises Dávila]]. He joins Chelsea on a five-year contract.<ref name="Dávila"/>
* 31 August 2011: The transfer deadline day sees [[Raul Meireles]] join from [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], whilst [[Yossi Benayoun]] and [[Patrick van Aanholt]] depart on seasonal loan deals. [[France national under-20 football team|France Under-20 international]] [[Gaël Kakuta]] joins [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on loan until 1 January 2012.
* 18 September 2011: Chelsea suffer their first defeat of the season, losing 1–3 to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at Old Trafford. [[Fernando Torres]] scored Chelsea's goal.
* 29 November 2011: Liverpool knock Chelsea out of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] at the Quarter Final stage, winning 2–0 at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. The loss is Chelsea's third in four games, and sixth of the season overall.
* 3 December 2011: Manager André Villas-Boas confirms that [[Nicolas Anelka]] and [[Alex (footballer, born June 1982)|Alex]] have been transfer listed, and banned from training with the first team, after handing in transfer requests to the club. Both will be allowed to resume full training if the transfer does not happen in the January transfer window. The announcement is made after the away match against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], which Chelsea win 3–0.
* 6 December 2011: Chelsea win their final [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League group stage|Champions League]] group game against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] 3–0 to secure progress to the knockout stages. [[K.R.C. Genk|Racing Genk's]] 1–1 draw against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] means that Chelsea top Group E.
* 12 December 2011: Chelsea become the first team in the 2011–12 edition of the Premier League to defeat leaders [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. Chelsea come from behind in a fiery encounter by goals from [[Raul Meireles]] and a late penalty by [[Frank Lampard]] to turn the deficit into a victory.
* 4 March 2012: Villas-Boas is sacked and removed of his duties by the director's board following a 0–1 defeat against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2633048 | title=Villas-Boas: his Chelsea time | publisher=Chelsea F.C | date=4 March 2012 |access-date=7 August 2013}}</ref> Italian first team assistant manager [[Roberto Di Matteo]] Is officially appointed as caretaker manager until the end of the season.
* 14 March 2012: Chelsea win their second match in the round of 16 of the [[UEFA champions league]] against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] with a 5–4 aggregate victory. [[Branislav Ivanović]] scores the winner in extra time to secure a spot in the quarter-finals. Following defeat of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] by [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] and defeats of the Manchester clubs in their respective [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] ties, Chelsea becomes the only remaining English representative in all European competitions.
* 18 March 2012: Chelsea progress to the [[FA Cup semi-finals#2010s|FA Cup semi-finals]] for a fifth time in seven years after beating [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] 5–2 at Stamford Bridge. [[Fernando Torres]] was the man of the match with two goals and two assists.
* 4 April 2012: Chelsea progress to the Champions League semi-finals for the sixth time in the past nine seasons after beating [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] 3–1 on aggregate.
* 15 April 2012: Chelsea progress to the FA Cup final for the third time in four seasons, courtesy of a 5–1 win against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. Controversy over Chelsea's second goal by [[Juan Mata]] adds to calls for goal-line technology.
* 24 April 2012: Chelsea progress to the Champions League final in spectacular fashion, drawing 2–2 with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at [[Camp Nou]] despite playing with ten men for more than two-thirds of the game. Chelsea win 3–2 on aggregate.
* 28 April 2012: Chelsea agree personal terms with [[Werder Bremen]]'s [[Marko Marin]]. He is set to join in the summer.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/28/chelsea-marko-marin-werder-bremen "Chelsea agree deal to sign Marko Marin from Werder Bremen"]. ''The Guardian''. 28 April 2012. Retrieved 4 August 2013.</ref>
* 5 May 2012: Chelsea win the FA Cup for the seventh time after beating [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 2–1 in the [[2012 FA Cup Final|Final]]. [[Didier Drogba]] scores in his fourth FA Cup Final – a new record.
* 19 May 2012: Chelsea win their first Champions League title, defeating [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] on penalties after a 1–1 draw in the [[2012 UEFA Champions League Final|Final]]. In doing so, Chelsea becomes the 22nd club to win the European Cup, the fifth English team and the first team from London to win the trophy.
